title: Commonwealth Credit Union - Zest AI Credit Underwriting Platform
content: Commonwealth Credit Union, a financial institution managing 2.2 billion dollars in assets, faced severe operational challenges due to high turnover rates among its experienced underwriting staff. To maintain relationship continuity and handle rising loan application volumes, the organization needed to optimize its credit underwriting process and provide a faster, more frictionless lending experience for its 120,000 members. To address these needs, Commonwealth Credit Union deployed Zest AI's automated credit underwriting platform. The deployed solution leverages advanced machine learning techniques to evaluate applicants, using a wider pool of data points from credit bureau reports to bypass the limitations of traditional credit scoring methods. This technology has successfully automated 70 percent to 83 percent of all consumer loan decisions, including auto loans, personal loans, and credit cards. Since integrating the system in 2021, the credit union has approved more than 324 million dollars in consumer loans, representing over 18,000 credit approvals. Furthermore, the quality of these loans has improved, with Commonwealth Credit Union reporting a 30 percent to 40 percent lower delinquency rate across portfolios compared to traditional credit scoring models.

title: HSBC - Dynamic Risk Assessment platform for anti-money laundering monitoring
content:
HSBC, one of the world's largest financial services organizations, faced significant challenges with its legacy rules-based anti-money-laundering systems. The bank was screening approximately 1.2 billion transactions monthly, but the rigid parameters resulted in a high volume of false positives. Investigators spent the vast majority of their time clearing these incorrect alerts, leading to investigator alert fatigue and slow detection times.

To resolve this issue, HSBC partnered with Google Cloud to develop and deploy its Dynamic Risk Assessment platform, also known as Anti Money Laundering AI. Rather than relying on rigid, human-authored rules, the system employs advanced machine learning algorithms to evaluate transactions. It analyzes transaction amounts, timing patterns, geographic locations, and behavioral indicators to build a probabilistic risk profile.

Following the deployment, HSBC reported that the AI-driven system achieved a 60% reduction in false positive alerts, allowing compliance teams to focus on high-priority cases. Additionally, the platform identified two to four times more suspicious activity than previous methods. This increased accuracy enabled HSBC to identify twice as much financial crime in its commercial banking operations and nearly four times as much across its retail banking operations. Detection times for suspicious accounts were also significantly accelerated, dropping to eight days after the initial alert.

title: Klarna - An OpenAI-powered customer service assistant
content: Swedish fintech firm Klarna faced high customer support volumes and rising costs across its global customer base. To address these issues, the company built and deployed an AI-powered customer service assistant in partnership with OpenAI. Utilizing generative conversational AI, the assistant was integrated into Klarna's customer chat application across 23 markets to handle inquiries about payments, refunds, and returns in over 35 languages. In its first month of launch, the AI assistant successfully managed 2.3 million conversations, representing 67 percent of all customer service chats and performing the equivalent workload of 700 full-time agents. Additionally, Klarna reported that the average resolution time plummeted from 11 minutes to under two minutes, and repeat inquiries dropped by 25 percent. Over the course of the deployment, these efficiencies contributed to a 40 percent reduction in customer service cost per transaction, from $0.32 in Q1 2023 to $0.19 in Q1 2025. This resulted in over $60 million in documented savings while maintaining customer satisfaction on par with human agents.

title: New American Funding - AI-powered account reconciliation and document processing
content:
New American Funding (NAF), a leading U.S. mortgage firm, faced significant operational bottlenecks in its accounting department due to the manual reconciliation of purchase advices. Accounting teams had to manually access multiple portals to retrieve, process, and reconcile a high volume of unstructured PDF documents in diverse formats from 40 to 50 different investor organizations. 

To modernize this workflow, NAF collaborated with evolv Consulting to deploy an automated account reconciliation solution. The system was built using evolv's Intelligent Document Processing (IDP) solution accelerator integrated with Snowflake's Cortex platform, utilizing custom large language models, DocumentAI, and Snowflake Arctic. This bespoke AI architecture automated the entire lifecycle of document retrieval, preparation, data extraction from diverse PDF templates, and ledger reconciliation under a secure governance framework. 

The deployment successfully eliminated manual bottlenecks and portal hopping. NAF reported that the AI solution reduced manual document processing time by over 80% and freed up 15 hours per week for strategic tasks. Furthermore, the accounting team can now process an average of more than six documents per minute, allowing workflows that previously required eight to ten hours to be completed in just six seconds with a 40% improvement in data accuracy.
